sessions.speaker: Joe Holmes
sessions.notes: Upgrading Democracy: lessons from Taiwan’s civic hackers, from g0v’s 2012 hackathons and the 2014 Sunflower occupation of the legislature to the government inviting them in to build vTaiwan. Joe showed how Pol.is maps opinion groups and finds “bridge” statements both sides agree on, the process that settled Taiwan’s Uber fight, and how a 2024 citizens’ assembly shaped its law on deepfake scam ads.

sessions.topic: How to learn in the age of AI
sessions.speaker: Vaughn Spurrier
Carson Sweet
sessions.notes: LLM Security Flyover: how refusals are supposed to work, until they don’t. Safety training only “paints” the parts of a model its examples reach, so most jailbreaks route around the refusal circuit through untrained regions (rare languages, past tense, personas) rather than breaking it. Carson also shared his Game of Life–style mouse colony simulation, which came up in questions (unrelated to the security talk): the game, a design article and the repo.

sessions.topic: How to make health decisions without data
sessions.speaker: Jason Itri
sessions.notes: No large randomized trial means no guideline, no insurance coverage and usually no prescription, even for treatments like testosterone or BPC-157 that can’t be patented and so rarely get one. Jason’s alternative: define the outcome you want to change, weigh mechanism and safety signals, set a prior, and run an N-of-1 trial (baseline, treatment, washout, rechallenge) to ask whether it works for you.

sessions.topic: Crazy alcohol regs of the U.S.
sessions.speaker: Sidd Dalal
sessions.notes: Two bottles, one maze: an Indian gin and an American whiskey land in a New Jersey warehouse, then hit 51 sets of rules — license, franchise and control states, who may ship spirits by mail, and residency limits on who can be a wholesaler. Ninety-odd years after Prohibition ended, it’s still why a California restaurant can’t simply buy the gin. The slides’ access code is becamp.
